subtopics.title: The Fixed Asset Note and What Moves

questions.question: Opening carrying value R1 080 000, additions R500 000, disposal at carrying value R90 000, depreciation R290 000. Closing carrying value is:
In the fixed asset note, additions enter and disposals leave at:
options: Both at selling price
Additions at cost; disposals at carrying value — and the two never swap
Additions at carrying value; disposals at cost
Both at market value

questions.question: The disposed vehicle had cost R300 000 and accumulated depreciation R210 000, and it sold for R75 000. The income statement shows:
options: A profit on disposal of R75 000
Nothing — disposals affect only the note
A loss on disposal of R15 000 — proceeds against the carrying value of R90 000
A loss on disposal of R225 000

questions.question: A question can leave any one cell of the note blank because:
options: The blank cell is always zero
The note need not balance
Students may estimate it
Every figure is chained to the others, so a missing figure is recoverable from the rest

subtopics.title: Age, Lifespan and the Replacement Question

questions.question: Equipment cost R1 200 000, is depreciated straight-line at 10 percent, and accumulated depreciation is R720 000. Its average age is:
options: Six years — accumulated depreciation divided by the annual charge of R120 000
Four years
Ten years
R720 000 divided by R1 200 000, so 0,6 years

questions.question: With a ten-year lifespan and six years consumed, the appropriate management response is to:
options: Stop depreciating the equipment
Plan and finance replacement now, across the remaining four years
Wait until year ten and then decide
Sell the equipment immediately at any price

questions.question: Additions of R500 000 against depreciation of R290 000 in the same year suggest:
options: The fleet is aging dangerously
Depreciation has been miscalculated
Assets are being renewed faster than they are consumed — the fleet is getting younger
The company is insolvent

questions.question: A business whose depreciation outruns its additions year after year looks profitable but is actually:
options: Growing its capacity
Improving its liquidity
Reducing its tax risk
Quietly eating its own capacity — breakdowns, downtime and big replacement bills lie ahead

questions.question: The strongest audit evidence that a vehicle exists is:
options: Physical inspection — the auditor finds the vehicle and matches it to the asset register
The depot manager's verbal assurance
A photograph supplied by the driver
An entry in last year's report

questions.question: Taking every tenth item from the asset register is:
options: Random sampling
Systematic sampling — orderly coverage of the population
Stratified sampling
Judgement sampling

questions.question: Weighting the sample toward the highest-value and most portable assets is justified because:
options: Those items are easiest to find
It reduces the sample size to one
The biggest rands and highest risks deserve the most testing
Managers prefer those items checked

questions.question: A well-written internal audit finding contains:
options: Only the name of the guilty employee
A summary of the company's history
The auditor's personal opinion of management
The gap between what should happen and what does, the risk in rands, and the recommendation that closes it

subtopics.title: The Internal and the External Auditor

questions.question: The internal auditor is appointed by, and reports to:
options: Management and the audit committee — as an employee working all year
The shareholders at the annual general meeting
SARS
The JSE

questions.question: The external auditor's scope is:
options: Every operational process in the company
The annual financial statements, examined for fair presentation and ending in a published opinion
Only the fixed asset register
Staff efficiency and morale

questions.question: Strong internal audit work affects the external audit by:
options: Replacing it entirely
Making it more expensive
Reducing the external testing needed — though the external auditor never simply adopts internal findings
Delaying the audit opinion

questions.question: The three layers of assurance, from inside out, are:
options: External audit, then internal audit, then controls
Internal audit daily, controls yearly, external audit continuously
Shareholders, directors, SARS
Internal controls operating daily, internal audit checking periodically, external audit verifying annually

questions.question: The five beats of the fixed asset note, in order, are:
options: Begin, buy, sell, wear, end
Buy, sell, begin, end, wear
Begin, wear, end, buy, sell
Sell, buy, wear, begin, end

questions.question: When the old bakkie is sold, the amount that leaves the note is:
options: The selling price
The R90 000 the books still carried — the selling price never enters the note
The original cost less the selling price
Whatever the buyer eventually pays

questions.question: A blank cell in the note is an invitation because:
options: Blank cells score full marks automatically
The question has abandoned that figure
The five beats are chained — any one can be rebuilt from the other four
It may be filled with any reasonable estimate

questions.question: The habit that prevents the classic mix-up is:
options: Round every figure to the nearest thousand
Record everything at selling price
Start from the closing balance
Things arrive at what they cost; things leave at what the books still carried

subtopics.title: How Old Is the Fleet, Really?

questions.question: R720 000 of wear gathered at R120 000 per year means the equipment is:
options: Six years old on average, with four years of its ten-year life left
Four years old with six left
Brand new
Past its lifespan already

questions.question: The four remaining years are called a countdown because:
options: Depreciation accelerates in the final years
Replacement must be planned and financed before the equipment dies — waiting for year ten means meeting the bill broke
The equipment must legally be scrapped in year ten
The books close in four years

questions.question: The cruel part of an aging fleet is that the aging years:
options: Show enormous losses
Require no depreciation
Look profitable, because so little is being spent on replacement
Attract higher insurance refunds

questions.question: Age and replacement figures must be read with caution because:
options: Depreciation is never accurate
Registers are usually falsified
Lifespans are fixed by law
They are averages across a class — one new bakkie and four wrecks can average out looking fine; only the asset register answers item by item

subtopics.title: The Inside Checker and the Outside Referee

questions.question: Naledi draws registrations from a hat on some days so that:
options: No depot can predict which vehicles will be checked
The sample is always the same
Only new bakkies are tested
The drivers can prepare their logbooks

questions.question: Naledi's evidence ranking puts seeing the bakkie herself above the depot manager's assurance because:
options: Managers are always dishonest
Evidence the auditor obtains directly and independently is stronger than verbal assurance
Bakkies are easier to photograph than managers
Assurance is not allowed in reports

questions.question: If the owner files Naledi's report and the fuel keeps vanishing, accountability lies with:
options: Naledi, for not fixing the problem herself
The drivers collectively
Management — internal audit reports weaknesses; acting on them is management's job
The external auditor

questions.question: The outside referee differs from Naledi in that she:
options: Works for the owner full-time
Checks depot efficiency in detail
Never reads Naledi's files
Is chosen by and reports to the people whose money is in the business, and rules only on whether the statements fairly show the truth
